claims.paraphrase: Page title.
A scaffolded site already has a design: Waymark wired into a chassis of plumbing.
A hand-built site has neither; it brings its own theme and delivery wiring.
Section heading.
The chassis holds plumbing including the feed and sitemap builders, runtime composition, and the token system.
Also in the chassis: prose foundations and composition primitives.
Everything outside the chassis is Waymark's own adapter config, chrome, values, and compositions.
A theme file reaches the chassis only through its seams: the alias in code or a relative CSS import.
Cairn's repo enforces the boundary on the showcase with a gate; a scaffolded site holds it as convention.
A re-skin never touches the chassis.
The token file declares design-scale keys with defaults; the engine's public stylesheet supplies the roles.
A theme imports the token file, then redeclares keys later; named daisyUI themes stay outside the chassis.
Section heading.
One file, the theme stylesheet, owns the look; the recipe is about fourteen values, light and dark.
The prose stylesheet needs no edits because it reads the same role tokens.
A status rebrand costs one fill per status; the engine derives each ink at half strength.
Two CI gates keep the recipe honest on the showcase; neither ships in a scaffold, while the three public rules do.
The site's check script runs the audit, where the three rules report as advisories.
Run the check script after a theme edit and compare by eye with the styleguide.
Section heading.
The styleguide route renders each registered directive, the type scale, and recipes against the live theme file.
Several theme relationships, such as the CTA ink and card border with shadow, are not evident from one hex value.
Layout changes need real entries and media; a clone has the markdown and manifest but not the pictures kept in R2.
Seed the local R2 simulator once per clone with the seeding command pointed at the deployed site.
Snippet running the seeding command against a deployed address.
Re-run only when the deployed library gains objects; the command is idempotent.
With nothing deployed there is nothing to seed; local admin uploads go straight to the local bucket.
After seeding, the dev script renders every page with real content and images.
Hot reload applies a stylesheet or component edit without a manual reload.
Advice on watching the dev terminal, testing structural changes, deferring the full gate, and checking viewports.
When settled, run the full checks, commit, push, deploy, and check the live site once.
Section heading.
The registry, chrome, compositions, and token-styled primitives are copy-in files a site owns with no version lock.
Extend the registry or add a composition as the showcase does for its home and article views.
Composition primitives expose their own per-primitive custom properties for instance overrides.
Section heading.
The chassis is generous and each file lists its dependents, keeping removals bounded.
The feed file has two dependents and can go with its routes; the content file serves six routes.
Consult the dependents table in the chassis README before removing a piece; a light theme may rebuild or drop any of it.
Section heading.
The styleguide renders every directive with no dangling token.
An AA contrast check on your edit passes in both light and dark.
The reading surface matches the rest of the page in contrast and rhythm with no separate CSS.
